To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a functional analysis of behavior, including dysfunctional behavior, can facilitate an understanding and assessment of the validity of animal models for psychopathologies; (2) the functional analysis of behaviors in animal models may facilitate a more systematic analysis and assessment of the psychopathology; and (3) a functional analysis can provide a more systematic approach to the development of animal models of psychopathology.
the functional analysis of behavior in animal models is crucial to the development of valid models of human psychopathologies.
the functional organization of behavior is a conserved characteristic of the nervous system across species, including humans.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding behavior, its organization, and its adaptive functions.
the development of a conceptual framework to evaluate the functionality of behavior in animal models of human psychopathology, and to use this framework to assess the validity of these models.
the development of translational models for human psychopathologies that are based on an analysis of behaviors and their functionality.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the functionality of behavior in translative models for psychopathologies can be a crucial element in the assessment of model validity.
animal models are not only necessary but also useful, but the usefulness of a model is not a function of the model itself, but rather of the way in which it is used.
a systematic analysis of the functionality of behavior is a crucial element in the translational research enterprise.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a functional approach to behavior can facilitate a translational research emphasis on the etiology, pathogenesis, and treatment of psychopathologies.

a systematic analysis of the functionality of behaviors in animal models can facilitate an assessment of model validity and may also provide insights into the etiology and treatment of psychopathology.
the study of behavior is essential in translational research.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the analysis of behavior in animal models of psychopathology can be greatly enhanced by a focus on the functionality of behaviors.

the analysis of behaviors that have been conserved across phylogenetically distant species may be a useful way to understand the biology of normal behavior, and that this may be particularly useful in understanding the etiology of psychopathologies.

, when a particular behavior has an identifiable function, it is more likely to be conserved across different species, including humans and nonhuman animals, and therefore more likely to be a valid model for a human disorder.
